name: Piracetam
sections: White crystalline powder, freely soluble in water; melting point 152 °C.

The first 'nootropic'; Giurgea coined the term in 1972. Approved in many European and Asian countries but not in the USA. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1964 by Corneliu E. Giurgea at UCB; marketed 1971.

Enhances neuronal membrane fluidity and cholinergic/glutamatergic neurotransmission; improves cerebral microcirculation by reducing platelet aggregation and red-cell rigidity. Used for cortical myoclonus and cognitive impairment. Receptor / target profile: Mechanism not fully defined: increases membrane fluidity, modulates AMPA and cholinergic transmission, reduces erythrocyte adhesion and platelet aggregation.
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax ~1 h. Not protein bound; not metabolised. Half-life ~5 h. Excreted unchanged in urine – adjust in renal impairment.
Vertigo of central or vestibular origin
Dyslexia in children (adjunct, with speech therapy)
Post-stroke aphasia and post-traumatic cognitive deficits (adjunct)
Cognitive disorders: 2.4–4.8 g/day in 2–3 divided doses
Cortical myoclonus: start 7.2 g/day, increase by 4.8 g/day every 3–4 days up to 24 g/day
Children (dyslexia, ≥8 years): 3.2 g/day in two divided doses
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl 50–79: ⅔ dose in 2–3 doses; 30–49: ⅓ dose in 2 doses; 20–29: ⅙ dose once; <20: contraindicated.
No adjustment unless renal impairment coexists.
Hypersensitivity to piracetam or pyrrolidone derivatives
Effect on platelet aggregation – caution with bleeding disorders, major surgery, anticoagulants
Avoid abrupt withdrawal in myoclonus (may trigger seizures)
Seizure exacerbation on abrupt withdrawal in myoclonus
Renal function; bleeding in at-risk patients.
Low toxicity; bloody diarrhoea and abdominal pain reported with very large doses. Supportive care; haemodialysis removes it.
Koskiniemi et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 1998 – effective adjunct in progressive myoclonus epilepsy.
Cochrane review (Flicker & Grimley Evans) – evidence for dementia/cognitive impairment inconclusive.
Do not stop suddenly if used for myoclonus
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
